plugins.name: scout
plugins.description: Repo-agnostic factory for support/investigation tooling for Claude Code teams — not a support tool itself. Developers install Scout in their repo and capture their team's tribal support knowledge as declarative 'playbooks' (YAML, no code); the resulting investigations are then consumable by ANY audience through ANY surface the repo supports — a Claude Code skill, the app's MCP server, or the app's own AI chat — so a business user with no repo access can still run a scoped, redacted investigation from the chat while a developer runs the same playbook with full evidence in Claude Code. Setup layer: /scout:setup (probe a repo — AI chat, MCP server, internal APIs, runbooks, data stores, auth/governance, and any existing investigation skills — and emit a Capability Manifest binding each abstract capability a playbook references to the repo's real endpoint/query/command + auth env var, mapping audience tiers developer/support/business/admin onto the repo's own roles so governance is inherited, not invented). Authoring layer: /scout:author (guided one-question-at-a-time wizard → one schema-validated playbook), /scout:harvest (auto-draft playbooks from existing runbooks, README troubleshooting, incident write-ups, and Makefile targets). Investigation layer: /scout:investigate (route an incoming ticket or run/record id to the matching playbook, gather evidence, emit a cited findings doc — then hand off to /agent-orch:make to fix a bug on the spot), /scout:explain (how-does-X-work from accumulated knowledge). Procedure layer: /scout:runbook (route a natural-language operation — 'promote to uat', 'sync secrets', 'refresh cache', 'run terraform apply' — to a matching kind: procedure playbook via the playbook INDEX filtered to procedures, bind its inputs, then execute its steps IN ORDER through the rails; every mutating step is needs-approval minimum with a preview + confirmation by an approval tier, followed by a verify step and rollback guidance on failure; a --dry-run mode emits a mutation-plan preview and executes nothing, and every run emits a cited run artifact). Playbooks are JSON-Schema-validated (draft 2020-12): typed inputs, safety-classified steps (api-read/query/shell-read/skill-call/guided-human/time-travel/note/diagnostic-query), confidence-tagged conclusions, mandatory redaction, keyword/signal triggers for routing. Complements, never replaces: a step can invoke a team's EXISTING skills (investigate-sentry, custom or tool-specific investigators) and use their output as evidence, and Scout wires playbooks into the app's own AI chat / MCP so scouting enriches their decisions too. Safe-command contract enforced by construction: read-only | needs-approval | forbidden, free-form prod queries forbidden, secrets used to connect but never read/echoed, outputs redacted before any surface returns them, dry-run preview before any step runs. Complements the team-work LLM wiki when present (ingests findings, answers /scout:explain via work-ask), degrades cleanly when absent. Reuses the agent-orch extensibility contract, worktree isolation, mcp-setup, and tracker-provider patterns.

plugins.name: team-work
plugins.description: Full SDLC plugin for Claude Code teams, now with an LLM-maintained knowledge wiki (an Open Knowledge Format / OKF v0.1 bundle: typed markdown concept pages, per-directory index.md navigation, okf_version at the bundle root) that can be published to GitHub Pages. Shift-left gates (requirements → agreement → handoff, all wiki-required): /work-analyze (analyze a requirements document against the ACTUAL codebase — auto-resolved from sibling repos — and the wiki's prior decisions; every requirement gets a verdict: BUILD AS WRITTEN / BUILD WITH CHANGES / RECOMMEND AGAINST / DEFER / NEEDS DECISION, backed by file:line evidence or a cited decision, with an alternative for anything recommended against; open questions routed to named owners by audience, plus risks, implicit scope, and what the release won't deliver), /work-signoff (review-meeting transcript → the concise agreed scope statement stakeholders sign; reconciles against the prior analysis, supersedes any earlier sign-off with a 'what changed since' section while keeping it citable, and splits open items into blocking vs non-blocking so the build can start honestly), /work-handoff (work plan + tracker issues + wiki → developer onboarding guide, with the dependency map READ from the tracker's real link graph rather than inferred; repo/stack mapping, document index with reading order, DoD, and a getting-unblocked path that leads with querying the wiki). Knowledge layer: /work-wiki (init/repair a configurable wiki root with qmd search; README.md catalog + OKF index.md nav + standard relative markdown links that render on GitHub and Obsidian; offers GitHub Pages hosting on finish), /work-ingest (classify a client call/doc, archive it verbatim+categorized under sources/ as an audit trail — converting PDF/xlsx/docx to markdown while preserving the original — then integrate into requirement/entity/concept/decision/incident pages where every claim cites its source via a relative markdown link), /work-ask (qmd hybrid search → cited answer → file it back so explorations compound), /work-lint (health-check: contradictions, stale claims, orphans, missing pages/cross-refs, broken/dangling links, legacy [[wikilinks]]/index.md, source gaps), /work-upgrade (migrate an older wiki to current conventions: index.md → README.md via git mv, rewrite [[wikilinks]] → relative markdown links, verify link integrity, plus an OKF v0.1 conformance pass — backfill `type`, generate index.md nav, add okf_version; idempotent), /work-publish (host the wiki as a MkDocs Material site on SS&C GitHub Enterprise Pages — pages.code.ssnc.dev/<org>/<repo>/ — with the SS&C Blue Stone look by default (SS&C Blue #0077C8 + Teal, Calibri typography, bordered tables, light/dark, from an embedded canonical extra.css so the brand applies even offline; opt-out to plain Material); scaffolding mkdocs.yml with docs_dir at the wiki root and auto-generated nav, requirements.txt, and a self-hosted GitHub Actions workflow deploying via gh-deploy to gh-pages; auto-enables Pages via the API once gh-pages exists and verifies the live site; warns that excluding sources/ breaks citation links and recommends restricting viewers instead; code.ssnc.dev only, idempotent), /wiki-source (turn a code repository into wiki knowledge: generate/refresh C4 docs in docs/c4/ via /agent-orch:c4, write a business-domain guide at docs/wiki/domain/ and a technical/DevSecOps reference at docs/wiki/technical/ cross-linked to existing repo docs, then /work-ingest the repo's markdown into the wiki; honors ingest_mode, commits in place), /wiki-source-branch (the same pipeline over the entire repo, committed on the current branch with no prompt/worktree/PR; no-ops without a wiki; run automatically by /agent-orch:make after committing code so the wiki tracks every feature). Planning→release: /work-prep (intake), /work-plan (Jira), /work-pop (pick items), /work-report (HTML report with top-of-page Jira status KPIs — Open/In Progress/In Review/Done/Blocked/Total/%Done — across all project issues, plus Recently Shipped panel), /work-recap (time-windowed Markdown + Bluestone PPTX recap of Jira, commits, and agent-orch sessions — every Jira entry is enriched with description, last comment + total count, attachments, and full metadata so stakeholders can read without clicking into Jira), /groom (worktree-based backlog grooming with Jira lifecycle; transitions tracking Jira to Done and produces a self-contained Markdown + Bluestone PDF report with description, last comment, comment count, attachments, and metadata for every groomed issue), /create-release (tags, dual release notes, PDFs, GitHub releases, optional Jira tickets), /plugin-feedback (structured feedback wizard → Jira ticket in AITOOLS). Opt-in extensibility framework (repo-level config under .claude/ssnc-team-work/ with before/replace/after agent hooks, skill hook points; zero behaviour change by default).

plugins.name: vault-orch
plugins.description: Provisions an Obsidian vault into any agent-orch repo so /make + /build sessions, business-requirement intake notes, and Jira tickets cross-link as a navigable knowledge graph. Principle: store the relationships, never the state — the vault owns immutable references (which sessions/requirements touch which ticket) and the requirement thinking; Jira keeps owning mutable status. The ticket layer is DERIVED (phantom graph nodes via frontmatter wikilinks + live Dataview queries), never a stored per-ticket note or sync script. Four skills: /vault-orch:init (provision .obsidian/ with userIgnoreFilters baked into app.json for multi-GB repos, Dataview, templates, 3 dashboards, git hygiene; refuses without ssnc-agent-orch/; idempotent), /vault-orch:backfill (idempotent variant-B frontmatter stamper — header-only diff, skips code/links, generic project-key regex, dry-run default, one mechanical PR), /vault-orch:intake (scaffold a requirement note that feeds team-work:work-prep/work-plan then /make), /vault-orch:exec-update (exec-altitude weekly summary written INTO the vault as a dated, Dataview-indexed, Mermaid-charted node; uses a reusable gather-activity.mjs seam work-recap can later adopt, and is differentiated from team-work:work-recap). A defensive Stop hook auto-promotes each finished session's prompt.md metadata into frontmatter, keeping the vault current with zero forking of the agent-orch skills.

plugins.name: meta-orch
plugins.description: Meta-orchestration layer above /agent-orch:make for coordinating MANY parallel Claude Code sessions against HUGE multi-epic work (1→35 epics, 5→1000+ stories) using GitHub Issues on code.ssnc.dev as shared state, without modifying agent-orch. Four skills form a pipeline: /meta-orch:design-tech-spec (staff/principal-level tech-spec design — runs /deep-research when available plus a relentless grill-me-style one-question-at-a-time Socratic interrogation that considers the existing codebase, all source, and a team-work /wiki if initialized; writes docs/tech-specs/000N-name.md), /meta-orch:design-tech-plan (decompose an approved spec into epics→tranches→gated stories, CREATE every GitHub epic/story issue via gh with an embedded ready-to-run /make-session prompt in each — epics can be epics-of-epics; install the concurrency lock workflow + labels; write docs/tech-plan/000N-name.md), /meta-orch:make-session (the ONLY worker skill and sole owner of GitHub story/epic state for a session: prints a HUGE RED 'do not start another /make-session yet' warning, finds an open + gate-open story scoped to an epic or across epics, asks the user to confirm, ATOMICALLY locks the issue the instant they confirm via a GitHub Actions concurrency workflow, flips to a GREEN 'you may start another now', pulls .meta-orch/session-guardrails.md into context, and hands prompt + guardrails to /agent-orch:make; heartbeats via rolling labels + pointer comment, never modifying agent-orch), and /meta-orch:coordinate-session (a coordinator that loops every N minutes — configurable, default 5 — reading in-progress issues + heartbeat labels, reading each active session's STATUS.md, and reporting per-epic/per-story status: who's working on what, how it's going, and what's open-gated to run; flags stale sessions and optionally opens the next tranche's gate). Concepts: epics (nestable), stories (one story = one /make-session = one PR), tranches (parallel-safe groups), gates (open/blocked to prevent merge conflicts), atomic locks, and heartbeats. Config in .meta-orch/config.md (session count default 5, loop interval, labels, lock workflow) and the operating contract in .meta-orch/session-guardrails.md — both auto-provisioned on first run. Concept guide: docs/meta-orch.md. For a team of N engineers each running 3–7 sessions across multiple epics with a single coordinator.
